name: ai-packs
description: Ready-to-use AI packs, one per job: Claude Code plugins and n8n workflows, each tested before release.

plugins.name: pr-squad
plugins.description: 8 Claude Code agents that review your branch before code review. Run /pr-squad:ship, or just ask for a PR.

plugins.name: invoice-chaser
plugins.description: 8 Claude Code agents that find the money freelancers are owed: bank reconciliation, tax and duplicate checks, one verified reminder per client. Run /invoice-chaser:chase, or just ask to chase your unpaid invoices.

plugins.name: post-recycler
plugins.description: 8 Claude Code agents that turn one post into 10 formats (X post and thread, Threads, Bluesky, carousel, Instagram, 30 s video, newsletter, quote card, story), then a script checks every limit and every number. Run /post-recycler:recycle, or just ask to repurpose your post.

plugins.name: deploy-doctor
plugins.description: One Claude Code skill that reads the logs of a failed deployment, names the cause, cites the line of code behind it, and gives the fix and how to verify it. Never calls a clean SIGTERM shutdown a crash. Just say your deploy crashed.

plugins.name: post-autopsy
plugins.description: One Claude Code skill and a Python script that measure which hooks, formats, weekdays and hours go with more of your LinkedIn impressions, with the number of posts and the median of each group. Never concludes on fewer than 5 posts. Just ask what works in your posts.

plugins.name: rule-guard
plugins.description: One Claude Code skill and one hook that check the rules of your CLAUDE.md on every git commit: real dangers (secret, private key, .env, DROP TABLE) block the commit, style rules only warn. Never blocks on its own failures. Just ask to turn your CLAUDE.md rules into checks.

plugins.name: quote-check
plugins.description: 2 Claude Code agents that check a freelance quote against the client's brief before you send it: what the brief asks and the quote forgets, the hidden work behind a line, and every calculation, taxes included. Run /quote-check:check, or just ask to check your quote.
